articles.title: The secret life of the scream park: fear, fainting, clowns – and ‘code brown’
articles.summary: At Norfolk’s ‘premier scare attraction’ there are ghouls, chainsaws, satanic cults and a haunted hospital. But what goes on behind the scenes? ‘We always say to the scare actors, you’re going to think the boys will be the worst.
body: This is part of the workplace induction at PrimEvil, one of many immersive “scream parks” that pop up across the UK in the lead up to Halloween. For about £40 a ticket, groups of all ages spend the night roaming themed attractions and being terrorised by actors and special effects. Though the risks are minimal, the spikes in heart rate are very real.

For Francis and the rest of the team, PrimEvil is months in the making. The nightly production involves more than 100 actors and dozens of crew, spread across six themed attractions, each drawing from familiar horror tropes – the scary clowns at the Circus of Terror, the cannibalistic trailer-dwellers over at Route 666, the satanic cult of The Offering. The winding routes are designed to disorient you with strobe lights, smoke machines, mirrored walls, hidden doors, false exits and unstable floors. But it’s down to the performers to bring the nightmare to life.

articles.title: I Love Boosters review – supercool outlaw women go shoplifting in Boots Riley’s frantic and funny caper
articles.summary: Demi Moore’s haute-couture maven attracts the attention of a gang of contemporary Robin Hood type clothes robbers in Riley’s fashion biz satire. Here is an entertaining, if very exhausting fantasy-caper about the fashion biz from Boots Riley, a madcap mile-a-minute melee of unadulterated…
body: She plays Christie Smith, a billionaire couture designer who has an office in a trendily designed city block which leans over at an experimental angle. Christie is the object of obsessive attention from “boosters”: supercool young outlaw women who, nettled by her arrogance, shoplift her clothes from upscale stores and sell them on at knockdown Robin Hood prices. They are Corvette (Keke Palmer), Sade (Naomi Ackie) and Mariah (Taylour Paige), the latter having the superpower of, by holding her breath, turning herself into a white woman who is less likely to be challenged in a store; an interesting metaphor for what Frantz Fanon might have called black skin, white masks.

For all their savvy, the boosters have a soft spot for certain men in their lives, notably a charismatic community leader called Dr Jack (Don Cheadle), who is running a friendship self-help scheme that is actually a fraudulent pyramid scam. And Corvette is entranced by a laidback charmer and oral sex enthusiast played by LaKeith Stansfield, who turns out to be a demonic male succubus.

articles.title: ‘Looming stone towers like Maya temples’: a hike through Snowdonia’s slate country
articles.summary: A new trail in the national park traces the legacy of Welsh industry, while offering some of the UK’s finest riverside and mountain walks. The vital moment comes a couple of hours into the walk. I drop down from a tussocky hill towards the village of Y Fron.
body: This is the Llwybr Llechi Eryri (Snowdonia Slate Trail), an 83-mile hike that follows a great loop around the national park, starting in Bangor and ending in Bethesda. It strings together a series of abandoned slate quarries with some of the finest riverside and mountain walking in the UK. I’m doing just three days, starting in Llanberis and heading to Betws-y-Coed via stops in Beddgelert and Llan Ffestiniog.

Beyond Y Fron village, I descend into my first quarry, and it proves to be a classic. This was once the Dorothea slate quarry, a vast abandoned complex of railways, cottages and chasms. I start exploring: tunnels, cuttings, huge looming stone towers like Maya temples, all overgrown with ash, birch and oak. What strikes me is the craftsmanship and precision in construction, each stone hand-fitted without mortar, all for workaday industrial buildings.
points: A new trail in the national park traces the legacy of Welsh industry, while offering some of the UK’s finest riverside and mountain walks.

articles.title: Rachel Roddy’s pasta with Senegalese-inspired ragu – recipe
articles.summary: A historical adventure deep in the very heart of pasta country in southern Italy unexpectedly unearths a sauce with roots in Senegal. About 30 kilometres south of Naples, the town of Gragnano is surrounded by the Monti Lattari mountain range – the limestone backbone of the Sorrento peninsula.
body: The natural slope of the terrain was fortuitous, because it allowed for the construction of a sequence of mills, which started in around 1263. During a visit to Gragnano last month, local historian Giuseppe Di Massa explained how it all worked; how gravity drove the flow of water from one mill to the next, in order to power vertical millstones – a system created for the inconsistent flow. The valley, with its clever water system, became known as the valley of the mills; its role milling grain, which arrived at the nearby port of Castellammare di Stabia, a vital operation to Naples and surrounding towns.

The activity of the 30 mills peaked during the 18th century, but another industry was growing, one that harnessed another natural aspect of the town: its climate. The temperature, humidity and sea breeze were ideal conditions for drying pasta.

articles.title: 30+ Best Brown Bags to Shop in 2026
articles.summary: Brown handbags are trending across the runways and celeb street style. Shop 30+ of our favorite styles, from Balenciaga’s Rodeo carryall to Coach’s Chelsea shoulder bag.
body: Brown bags have been trending for a while—and as the fall 2026 runways proved, they’re back once again with serious staying power. As the styles spotted at Balenciaga, Loewe, and Miu Miu begin rolling into stores, rich earthy hues are shaping up to be this season’s most versatile neutral. Celebrities have also been out in full force, carrying these reliable, goes-with-everything styles on the streets throughout Fashion Month and in their own off-duty wardrobes. Consider this your cue to swap your go-to black bag for something a little warmer.

Miu Miu’s bags became instant must-haves on the runway. Both the Vivant and Pocket styles in cognac have become steadfast companions for Gigi Hadid, accompanying her on travel days and city strolls, while Alexa Chung has recently been spotted carrying the top-handle silhouette in rich chocolate on numerous occasions.

Balenciaga’s Rodeo bag also made an appearance on the fall 2026 catwalk—and has found a devoted fan in Sarah Pidgeon, who regularly carries the burnished brown iteration in her everyday life. Most recently, she wore it to the house’s Paris show, styling it with a contoured leather jacket, bootcut jeans, and pointy pumps.

articles.title: The 9 Best Airbnbs in Madrid for a Trip to Spain’s Buzzy Capital
articles.summary: Heading to Spain's capital? Book an Airbnb in Madrid and immerse yourself in the rich culture of the city—start with one of our nine favorites.
body: Spain’s capital is in the middle of a glow-up. You might have noticed more of your friends and family visiting; you might have also noticed that everyone seems to have only positive things to say about it. Madrid has always been a tourist favorite, but in 2026, a number of new openings, ambitious projects, and prestigious exhibitions have elevated it further.

Unlike many other capitals, where residential areas are usually found outside of the city’s main sights, here, those neighborhoods are built in and around all the sight-seeing big-hitters. Staying in an Airbnb in Madrid gives visitors the best of both: Local markets and restaurants are on your doorstep, and all the places you want to tick off your itinerary are nearby.

You’ll know you’ve arrived in the heart of historic Madrid before you even enter this 18th-century home; its ornamental facade and antique (but functional) elevator leading the way to the grand five-bedroom apartment.

articles.title: For Rosalía, No Bag Is Too Big, No Ballet Pump Too Bitchy
articles.summary: Out and about in New York City, Rosalía continues to expand her penchant for balletcore with outsized accessories and towering footwear.
body: Rosalía has a lot of baggage—and even more shoe. The Spanish pop star has never been one to do things by halves. Not when it comes to her music, and certainly not when it comes to fashion; especially not when it comes to accessories. Spotted out and about in New York City, the singer appeared to be carrying everything but the kitchen sink in an absolutely gargantuan leather bag, while teetering along in a pair of ballet shoes that took the humble flat to dizzying new heights. Traveling light? Not in Rosalía’s vocabulary.

Not content with an ordinary pair of ballet flats, Rosalía—who has been performing en pointe—opted for a pair of pale pink satin ballet platforms from Junko Shimada’s spring 2009 collection, with crisscrossing ankle ribbons, exaggerated black platforms, and transparent heels. The shoes have a fab pop cultural pedigree, too: Lady Gaga wore the shoes back in 2009, when her own penchant for architectural, gravity-defying footwear was in full swing. 15-plus years later, they look every bit as wonderfully impractical.

articles.title: Even for Desperate Restaurants, Fake Reviews Just Aren’t Worth It
articles.summary: When Yelp was first launched in 2004, it flopped. The company’s initial model of an email-based referral service failed to take off until its creators realized users were taking the platform into their own hands; in lieu of sending one another recommendations via email chain, they began using a…
body: It’s been over 20 years since Yelp was founded. At its best, the platform still feels like a place where the voices of hungry, curious diners can share their personal experiences and offer recommendations and tips; at its worst, it feels like a bloated repository for reviews filled with misdirected anger, unreasonable expectations, or else completely fake customer reviews. Initially, unsubstantiated and unreliable reviews were more often written by a person — either someone from the business itself, or paid by the business; now, a fake review can be penned by a paid influencer, a detailed generative AI prompt, or purchased from third-party agencies that will produce fake bot reviews in bulk.

Fake reviews were perhaps inevitable. Bot-driven comments became ubiquitous during an overripe moment in the untamed internet’s lifespan. But how does a restaurant shamed for gamifying its reviews — even if it was, presumably, out of desperation in a tough economic landscape — regain customers’ broken trust?
… The offending restaurant’s foot traffic went down by 8 percent, and dipped even lower around the holidays, a time when would-be diners rely even more on Yelp.

articles.title: The Hot List: 20 Must-Have Pieces, According to Instagram’s Favorite Fashion Sourcer
articles.summary: Gab Waller’s monthly cheat sheet of things to shop now before the most dreaded three words in online shopping appear (“out of stock”).
body: We’re officially in Q4 and in Gab Waller world, that means only one thing: our busiest season has begun! With fall in full swing (in most places, certainly not here in LA!) and the holiday season upon us, requests are coming through stronger than ever.

Multiple brands continue to dominate as my most requested: Chanel and Celine are the top two, with Saint Laurent, Prada, and The Row right behind them. We’re going to cover a lot of pieces from them in this month’s column. I’ve really enjoyed seeing Celine take over this past year, for it to be in the #2 spot is a clear signal of what I anticipated early on: it’s the year of Celine and Michael Rider!
If there is one fall item that you need, let it be a velvet blazer Magda Butrym. Her now iconic peplum style with structured shoulder pads is one of my top wardrobe must-haves. This will sell out.
Prada’s best selling pouch bag is now available in printed calf hair! Guaranteed to be highly coveted, I’m ready to see the influx of sourcing requests.

articles.title: 9 Best Hotels in Rio de Janeiro for a Taste of the Carioca Lifestyle
articles.summary: From grand hotels on Copacabana to intimate retreats in Santa Teresa, these stays capture Rio’s singular mix of beach life, Brazilian design, and warm hospitality.
body: “I live where you vacation” takes on a whole other meaning when, like me, you're based in Rio de Janeiro. I live smack in the middle of South America ’s two hottest beaches—Copacabana and Ipanema—but it’s not the ocean that keeps me in Brazil's buzziest city. It’s the life that happens around it. It’s the sound of the first coconuts being cut open on the beach in the early morning, the sight of barefoot surfers passing beneath my window, and the honey-like melody of bossa nova flowing from a nearby beach kiosk. Not everyone can live here, of course. But luckily, the best hotels in Rio de Janeiro give you a good taste of what it feels like to be a local in Brazil’s most exciting metropolis.

articles.title: The 38 Best Restaurants in Barcelona, According to a Local Food Guide
articles.summary: From Barcelona’s towering churches and bustling avenues to the sun-drenched beaches and idyllic plazas, it’s obvious why this city captures visitors’ hearts. You can also eat incredibly well here, and often for not very much money — though Barcelona loves a tasting menu and the World’s 50 Best…
body: Start with some classic tapas and paella (both great but neither entirely Catalan) and be sure to seek out local gems like bittersweet vermouth, seasonal seafood, and homestyle Catalan cuisine. But after writing and revising this list for nearly a decade, I have to insist you don’t overlook the city’s burgeoning global cuisines; save room for Calabrese paninis, Northeast Asian sharing plates with natural wines, towering fried chicken sandwiches, South Indian fish stews, and nose-to-tail yakitori.

We update this list quarterly to make sure it reflects the ever-changing Barcelona dining scene. Our write-ups include insider tips from our experienced writers and editors, as well as a rough range of pricing for each destination — ranging from $ for quick, inexpensive meals with dishes largely under $10 (or the equivalent in euros), to $$$$ for places where entrees exceed $30.

New to the map in October 2026: Lluritu, a Mediterranean marisquería with three locations across the city; a parallel universe of Catalan culinary history in a former water bottling plant at Franca; and the trendy modern Catalan cuisine of Manda Huevos.
